claims.text: Youth is no longer considered a prerequisite for subjective well-being.
Modest aspirations are no longer considered a prerequisite for subjective well-being.
Demographic factors have small overall effects on subjective well-being.
Subjective well-being consists of separable components including life satisfaction, pleasant affect, and unpleasant affect.

evidence.description: A number of his conclusions have been overturned: youth and modest aspirations no longer are seen as prerequisites of SWB.
A number of his conclusions have been overturned: youth and modest aspirations no longer are seen as prerequisites of SWB.
As we shall see, demographic factors have surprisingly small effects on SWB, but these effects may depend on the personalities of those individuals being studied.
In the past, many researchers have treated SWB as a monolithic entity, but it is now clear that there are separable components that exhibit unique patterns of relations with different variables.

methodologies.name: Literature Review
methodologies.description: A comprehensive review of theoretical approaches and empirical findings on subjective well-being over three decades.

limitations.text: The causal direction of demographic correlates such as marriage and income remains unconfirmed and uncertain.
The psychological processes responsible for adaptation to good and bad circumstances are poorly understood.
Prior research frequently treated subjective well-being as a monolithic entity rather than investigating its distinct components.

future_work.text: Examine the causal direction of the correlates of happiness through more sophisticated methodologies.
Focus greater attention on Person X Situation interactions between internal factors (such as personality traits) and external circumstances.
Understand adaptation processes by examining how habituation, coping strategies, and changing goals influence adaptation.
Refine theories to make specific predictions about how input variables differentially influence the separate components of subjective well-being.
